chunks: What al-Shaykh — may Allah the Exalted strengthen him — informed me, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yahya, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, on the authority of Ayyub ibn Nuh, on the authority of Safwan, on the authority of Isma'il ibn Jabir, who said:
I said to Abu 'Abd Allah (AS): [What is] the water that nothing can make impure? He said: 'Two cubits in depth, by one cubit and a span in width.'

key_terms.ذِرَاعَانِ: two cubits (dual of dhira', a linear measure of approx. 45–50 cm; specifying depth)
key_terms.سَعَتُهُ: its width/extent (the lateral dimension of the water body)
key_terms.شِبْرٍ: a span (distance from tip of extended thumb to tip of little finger, approx. 22 cm; specifying width)
key_terms.عُمْقُهُ: its depth (the vertical dimension of the water body)
key_terms.يُنَجِّسُهُ: renders it ritually impure (Form II verb from najasa; the question targets the threshold at which water resists contamination)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum depth and width of water that cannot be made ritually impure according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: Isma'il ibn Jabir asked Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) about the minimum quantity of water that cannot be rendered ritually impure by any contaminating substance. The Imam defined it as two cubits (dhira') in depth and one cubit and one span (shibr) in width — this is the classical Shia jurisprudential definition of a 'kurr' body of water, a central concept in the law of taharah governing which water remains valid for ritual use despite contact with najasah.
